chapter: Duke, Gensel and the later years
title: Tick-Tock in Boston, Newport and the road
summary: The summer-long Boston residency, Newport, Providence, Lennie's and Montreal.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: So I talked to George about that, and he said, "Yeah, that's a good idea." So I got booked into the Tick-Tock in Boston to play for two weeks, and the first night I opened there the guy talked to me and asked me would I like to stay there for all summer. So I didn't have no other place to go. I said, "Well, why not? Yeah, okay." So he hired me to stay for the summer. In the meantime, I had played just one set, and he liked the way I conducted my business and so forth. So he said, "How would you like to stay here all summer," so I...

Anyway, it was a nice club, where they had music, they had the girls come in and do a dance. So it was very nice. In fact, I enjoyed playing there, because they had a helluva crowds coming in. We stayed there all summer.

So I went to... What's the name of this club in... I ain't got it together. It ain't working right today. I'm trying to think of the name of this town, because I played there, I went there from Boston... Kings and Queens in Providence..
But when did you play the Festival with that group and Phil Porter? Was it that same year, up at Newport? I remember you playing there.

Yeah, we played Newport, and then we played... Oh, we played Newport while we were at the Tick-Tock. But shortly after that we played in Providence. So when we left Boston, we went down to Providence.
Then we went back up in Boston to Lennie's. Then we went out to Columbus to play the Ohio Festival. Then after that we had a gig up in Montreal at some joint there... I can't remember...
It was some joint, some club up in Montreal. And we stayed there for three weeks, and then I jumped from there back down to the Kings and Queens.
Who was in the group besides you and Phil? Who was the drummer?
Candy Finch. It was a helluva little combo. We really got tied up in...
